answer: For a poll on a pearl and cedar sculpture at the forge, the server checks election-bound signatures and ledger history. It counts each coin once, weighted by full days continuously held by its signer during the 30 days before the snapshot; invalid or reused coins are rejected. More coin-days require more coins or holding time, potentially tying up capital. Existing or borrowed holdings can qualify, wealth can dominate, and coins do not identify people.
